name: Chat with global news and save articles to Google Sheets with Webz.io and GPT-4.1-mini

parameters.content:
## Chat with global news and save articles to Google Sheets with Webz.io and GPT-4.1-mini

### Who's it for

Researchers, journalists, and analysts who want to interrogate current events in plain language, compare coverage across sources and countries, and keep the articles worth keeping. Useful when you do not know the right query yet.

### How it works

1. You ask a question in the chat panel.
2. **Answer the news question** plans its research with the **Plan the research** Think tool, then runs one or more Webz.io searches through the MCP Client Tool — narrowing with filters such as language, country, date range, sentiment, category, domain, ticker, person, organization, and location, and cross-checking significant claims across more than one source.
3. **Conversation memory** keeps the thread, so you can narrow or pivot across turns without repeating yourself.
4. When you say "save these", the agent appends each article to your **Reading list** spreadsheet — `saved_at`, `title`, `publisher`, `url`, `note` — so a good research session leaves you with more than scrollback.
5. The agent cites a source URL behind every claim, and says so plainly when a search turns up nothing.

### How to set up

1. On **Webz.io news search**, create a **Bearer Auth** credential and paste your Webz.io API token as the bearer token.
2. On **OpenAI Chat Model**, add your OpenAI credential.
3. On **Reading list**, connect your Google account, pick a spreadsheet and tab, and give the tab the headers `saved_at`, `title`, `publisher`, `url`, `note`.
4. Open the chat panel at the bottom of the canvas and ask a question.

### Requirements

- A Webz.io API token from [webz.io](https://webz.io)
- An OpenAI API key, or any other tool-calling chat model
- A Google account for the reading list (or delete the **Reading list** node to chat without one)

### How to customize

Edit the agent's system message to pin a beat, a language, or a set of trusted domains so you need not repeat it every turn. Swap **Conversation memory** for Redis or Postgres memory to keep history across restarts, or point **Reading list** at Notion or Airtable instead.

### Try asking

- What are people saying about EU AI Act enforcement this month?
- Compare how US and UK outlets covered the latest Fed decision.
- Find negative coverage of airline safety in the last week, English only, then save the three most serious to my reading list.

[Setup notes and full filter reference](https://github.com/Webhose/webz-news-search/blob/main/n8n/README.md)

### 1. Ask a question

Open the chat panel at the bottom of the canvas and type in plain language.

Add a **Chat Trigger** webhook later if you want to embed this on a site.

### 2. The research agent

It plans with the Think tool, runs as many searches as the question needs, compares coverage across sources, and cites a URL for every claim.

Say "save these" and it appends the articles to your reading list.

Edit the system message to pin a beat, a language, or a set of trusted domains.

### 3. Model, memory, and three tools

**OpenAI Chat Model** needs your OpenAI key, or swap the node for any other tool-calling model. **Conversation memory** keeps the thread within a session; use Redis or Postgres memory to survive restarts.

**Plan the research** is a Think tool: it gives the agent scratch space to choose angles and filters before spending search credits.

**Webz.io news search** needs a *Bearer Auth* credential holding your Webz.io API token. Leave *Tools to Include* set to **All** — the server exposes a single tool.

**Reading list** needs a Google Sheets credential plus a spreadsheet with the headers `saved_at`, `title`, `publisher`, `url`, `note`. The agent only writes to it when you explicitly ask to save. Delete the node to chat without it.

options.systemMessage:
You are a news research assistant with access to Webz.io global news search, a think tool for planning, and the user's reading list spreadsheet.

## Research method

Before the first search on any non-trivial question, use the think tool to plan: what angles matter, which filters narrow the noise, and what would confirm or contradict the obvious answer. Then search — more than once when the question calls for it. Comparing countries, outlets, or time periods means one search per side, not one blended search.

Always search before you answer. Never rely on your own knowledge of current events, and never invent an article, a publisher, or a URL. Report only what the tool returns, and cross-check significant claims across at least two different source domains when coverage allows.

## Using the search tool

The search tool accepts filters, so use them rather than stuffing keywords into the query. Useful ones are days, language, country, sentiment, category, domain, exclude_domain, ticker, person, organization, location, and topic, plus k to control how many results come back.

Filter value formats matter: language takes full names such as english or french, country takes uppercase ISO-2 codes such as US or DE, and ticker takes uppercase symbols such as NVDA. Omitting days searches the last 7 days.

Put the subject in the query argument, not in the topic filter. When a question is vague, run a broad search first and then narrow with filters based on what comes back. If a search using category or sentiment returns nothing, retry once without those filters before giving up.

## The reading list

Only write to the reading list when the user explicitly asks to save something. Call the tool once per article, with the exact title, publisher, and URL from the search results and a one-sentence note on why it was saved. Confirm what was saved afterwards.

## Answering

Cite the URL for every claim. Point out when sources disagree instead of averaging them. If the search turns up nothing relevant, say so and suggest a different angle instead of guessing.
